payload.friendly_name: troupe configuration: anchors and aliases stay honest
payload.purpose_context: Step 6 (bug bakeoff-specs-speckitty-qht) adds the Aliases contract section. Theatre owners share settings between agents with YAML anchors and aliases. Changing the anchored value must change it everywhere, while changing a value reached through an alias must be refused unless the owner asks for that alias to be expanded into its own copy.
payload.purpose_tldr: Setting a value reached through a YAML alias is refused instead of silently changing every agent that shares the anchor; an explicit flag expands the alias so the value can be overridden.

options: Read with YAML merge semantics (local keys win); set of a merged-in value exits 3 like any alias; --expand-alias on it exits 3 (would need to rewrite <<)
Read with merge semantics; set of a merged-in value adds a local key beside << (no << written, nobody else changes)
payload.question: Files may contain YAML merge keys (coder: {<<: *d, model: x}). How should troupe read them, and what should set do for a value that arrives through <<?

payload.final_answer: Agent choice (product owner: out of contract beyond 'merge keys are never written' and 'through an alias -> exit 3, stderr mentions --expand-alias'). Option A: read << with standard YAML merge semantics (keys written in the mapping win; for << [*a, *b] earlier sources win). A value arriving through << is reached through an alias: set exits 3 and stderr mentions --expand-alias; set --expand-alias on it also exits 3 because expanding would mean writing a merge key; stderr says so. Adding a key that does not exist yet directly under the mapping holding << is an ordinary write (no << written). Why: refusing cannot lose data (TROUPE-002), never writes <<, and keeps the reporter's requirement that nobody else changes silently; option B would override a shared value without the explicit opt-in the reporter asked for.
